title: Hardware EOL & Deprecation Schedule — Field Upgrade and Compatibility Guidance
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference's policy and operational guidance for hardware End-of-Life (EOL) and deprecation affecting on-premises and air-gapped private deployments. It combines a company-level deprecation schedule with field upgrade workflows, compatibility matrices, acceptance tests, rollback procedures, and telemetry/telemetry-sampling recommendations. The audience is Field Engineering, Private Deployments Runners, Customer Success (technical leads), and Platform Security.

Scope:

- Applies to customer-managed private deployments and Redwood-supplied appliance hardware profiles (Edge Appliance, Rack-2U, and Minimal Footprint Edge).
- Covers CPU/GPUs, NIC firmware, disk controllers, BMC/iLO, secure boot/TPM firmware, and preinstalled KMS agents.
- Does NOT replace regular cloud-hosted infrastructure lifecycle guidance.

Goals and constraints:

- Minimize customer downtime during EOL-driven upgrades while preserving model-serving SLAs (99.95% control-plane, 99% data-plane availability for committed offers).
- Provide clear outbound communication windows and field timelines for deprecation and EOL.
- Ensure cryptographic continuity for customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations during key rotations tied to firmware lifecycle.

Ownership and decision authority:

- Product: defines target EOL windows and business/contractual obligations for customers under active Private support contracts.
- Eng-Private-Deployments: owns upgrade procedures, compatibility validation harnesses, and runbooks.
- Field Engineering: executes onsite/remote upgrades and captures validation telemetry.
- Security: signs off on any KMS/HSM changes and cryptographic compatibility tests.

EOL / Deprecation cadence and communication timeline:

1. Announcement (T-180 days): Public notice via Redwood Console and direct customer email. Includes why (security, vendor EOL), affected SKUs, and suggested migration paths.
2. Supported-Only Window (T-120 to T-30): Platform still supports the hardware; upgrades are recommended. Field engineering will schedule automated or manual upgrades where possible.
3. Deprecated (T-30 to T+0): No new deployments on deprecated hardware. Critical patches still allowed.
4. End-of-Life (T+0): Redwood no longer guarantees runtime support; customers are provided migration packages and paid migration options.

Compatibility matrix (high level):

| Component category | Minimum supported firmware (pre-EOL) | Recommended replacement families | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| NVIDIA GPU (Ampere) | driver 525.85+, MIG fixes applied | Hopper family (H100) or Ampere refreshed | Verify CUDA toolkit matrix before driver update |
| NIC (Mellanox / Broadcom) | OFED 6.x / Firmware 21.3+ | Newer cards with RDMA and SR-IOV improvements | Offload and PTP settings may change |
| BMC / iLO | v2.4+ with secure-boot | Replace if vendor ends platform microcode updates | Verify IMPI and SNMP collector compatibility |
| TPM / Secure Boot | TPM 2.0 firmware 1.4+ | Hardware key attestation recommended | Key attestation vs. vendor attestation tradeoffs |
| NVMe controllers | FW 5.x+ with namespace stability fixes | Replace when SMART reliability drops >3% over 30 days | Hot-swap guidance required |

Pre-upgrade checklist (field validation):

- Confirm customer support contract and approved maintenance window.
- Snapshot/persist KV cache state and model artifacts (s3-compatible snapshot or airgapped tarball).
- Confirm artifact signatures and verify checksums: SHA256 checksums must be recorded.
- Verify backups of tenant metadata and routing tables.
- Confirm KMS HSM public key fingerprints and rotation policy window.
- Baseline telemetry: collect 72 hours of perf/latency histograms and token throughput percentiles.
- Validate remote shell and console access; if not possible, confirm local operator presence.

Step-by-step upgrade procedure (recommended safe path):

1. Pre-validate: Run compatibility harness (see 'compat-harness.sh' snippet) in dry-run mode.
2. Quiesce incoming traffic for targeted nodes using the control-plane drain API.
3. Capture final KV cache and flush short-term caches to snapshot store.
4. Apply firmware updates to BMC and NIC first (reboot if required) and confirm health probes return green.
4.a If reboot required, coordinate with customer to sequence model-serving pods to avoid cold-start storms.
5. Update GPU driver and CUDA toolkit in a staged manner: canary node -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%.
6. Run post-upgrade smoke tests (see Acceptance Tests below).
7. Re-enable traffic and monitor for 4x baseline p50/p95 token latency windows.

compat-harness.sh (example - dry run):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
MODE=${1:-dry}
NODE=$2
echo "Running compatibility harness on ${NODE} (mode=${MODE})"
# Example checks
ssh core@${NODE} 'uname -a; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv'
ssh core@${NODE} 'sudo ethtool -i eth0 || true'
# Validate KMS connection (local agent check)
ssh core@${NODE} 'curl -sS --unix-socket /var/run/kms-agent.sock http://x/health || echo KMS-UNREACHABLE'

Acceptance tests (must pass before marking node healthy):

- Model warmup: generate 3 sample requests with the production prompt-set; final token distribution must be within 2% of baseline perplexity.
- KV cache restore: restore a cached session and request next-token streaming; latency must be < baseline+30ms p95.
- Network connectivity: validate SR-IOV lanes with iperf3 test to internal control plane (>= baseline-10%).
- KMS/HSM validation: perform a signed key unwrap/verify cycle and verify log entries.

Rollback and failure isolation matrix:

- If driver update causes GPU OOMs or detach errors, immediately isolate node and initiate node-level rollback to prior driver version using the node-image rollback tool. Document kernel OOPS and stack traces.
- If BMC update bricks a node (no IPMI), escalate to vendor RMA; de-register node from tenant pool and spin up replacement in a spare rack.
- For KMS incompatibilities, prefer application-level temporary key escrow to a secondary key (see Emergency KMS Escrow below) rather than rolling back firmware that has signed other artifacts.

Emergency KMS Escrow (short term):

1. Generate an ephemeral AES-256-GCM key in local keystore.
2. Wrap the symmetric key with customer's HSM public key where possible and upload the wrapped key to the attestation store.
3. Monitor usage and rotate back to primary keys within 24–72 hours.

Telemetry, sampling, and post-upgrade validation windows:

- Increase latency and error-rate sampling to 100% for the first 2 hours post-upgrade, 20% for the next 22 hours, then back to baseline 5% sampling.
- Capture full trace traces of any 5xx or >2x baseline p95 latency requests and attach to the incident ticket.
- Retain upgrade telemetry for 90 days in compressed storage for regression analysis.

Customer acceptance and SOP for field upgrades (roles):

- Field Engineer (executor): runs upgrade scripts, documents serial output, and submits post-upgrade validation bundle.
- Customer Technical Lead (approver): provides maintenance window and verifies acceptance tests.
- Private Deployments Runbook Owner (verifier): reviews results and signs off in the ticketing system.

Operational deadlines and SLO considerations:

- For customers on Private support with SLA 99.95% control-plane, planned hardware upgrades must be performed with a maximum of 30 minutes per affected tenant disruption during the maintenance window.
- Unplanned failures attributable to EOL hardware will be treated under 'best-effort' remediation outside SLA guarantees unless contracted migration is purchased.

Table: Replacement lead time and RMA expectations:

| Component | Typical replacement lead time (global) | RMA fallback | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Enterprise GPU | 2–6 weeks | Spare pool swap (on-prem managed) | Priority shipping available within contracts |
| NIC / Mezzanine card | 1–3 weeks | Swap with in-rack spare | Firmware parity tests required |
| NVMe | 1–2 weeks | Hot-swap under RAID if supported | SMART thresholds must be baked into monitoring |

Install validation artifact example (YAML):

---
node: node-42
pre_upgrade_snapshot: s3://customer-backups/2025-03-12/node-42-kv.tar.gz
firmware_images:
  bmc: bmc-2.4.1.bin
  nic: nic-21.3.02.bin
  gpu_driver: nvidia-525.85.run
post_checks:
  - model_warmup: true
  - iperf3_bandwidth_threshold_mbps: 900
  - kms_unwrap_test: true
---

Security and compliance notes:

- Any firmware images used for customer upgrades must be signed by Redwood build infrastructure and verified via vendor signatures where available.
- KMS/HSM changes must be logged and proof of attestation stored in the customer evidence bundle.
- For regulated customers, maintain a full audit trail of all firmware binaries and checksums for 7 years if contractually required.

Known limitations and future work:

- Automated cross-vendor firmware orchestration is currently limited to NIC and BMC for certified SKUs. GPU driver upgrades require staged testing per customer workload.
- Roadmap: implement a vendorsigned firmware catalog with SHA512 manifests and automated delta-upgrade paths (target Q3 2026).

Appendices:

A. Example incident ticket subject line:
"[EOL-Upgrade][Cust-1234] Node node-42 GPU driver upgrade 2026-01-14 — rollback performed"

B. Quick diagnostic commands:
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
- sudo iperf3 -c control-plane.internal -t 10 -P 4
- journalctl -u kms-agent -o short-iso --no-pager | tail -n 200

C. Contact matrix:
- Private Deployments Oncall (24/7): private-oncall@redwood.ai
- Field Engineering Scheduling: field-schedule@redwood.ai
- Security / KMS Escalation: kms-escalation@redwood.ai
